sources.entry: API management is the process of creating and publishing application programming interfaces (APIs), enforcing their usage policies, controlling access, nurturing the subscriber community, collecting and analyzing usage statistics, and reporting on performance.

summary.name: API (Wikipedia article)
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia's encyclopedia article explaining what an application programming interface (API) is, its history, types, design, and documentation.
use_cases: learning the history of application programming interfaces
comparing web APIs with library APIs
reviewing API design and documentation principles
summary.what_it_does: This is an encyclopedia article, not a software tool. It defines an API as a connection or interface between computers or programs, and distinguishes it from a user interface. It covers API types, including libraries and frameworks, operating systems, remote APIs, and web APIs. It also describes design principles such as information hiding, API release policies (private, partner, public), and documentation practices. It traces the history of the term from the 1940s EDSAC library to REST and the Oracle v. Google copyright case.
notable: Covers the history of APIs from 1940s EDSAC subroutine libraries to modern web APIs
Explains API release policies: private, partner, and public
Summarizes the Oracle v. Google Java API copyright dispute
caveats: Describes concepts rather than a specific product, so it has no tool features to use
Some sections are dated; the article notes content as of 2021
